title: Anthropic prices initial public offering
author: surprisetalk
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Today Anthropic, PBC priced its initial public offering of its Class A common stock at $83.00 per share. The offering consists of 980,000,000 shares of Class A common stock, 956,351,354 of which are being sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 of which are being sold by certain selling stockholders. Anthropic will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling stockholders.The shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19, 2026 under the symbol “ANT.” The offering is expected to close on November 20, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions. In addition, Anthropic has granted the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 147,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock.A registration statement relating to these securities was declared effective by the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 18, 2026. The offering is being made only by means of a prospectus. Copies of the final prospectus may be obtained, when available, from: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 200 West Street, New York, NY 10282, by telephone at (866) 471-2526, or by email at prospectus-ny@ny.email.gs.com; or Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, Attention: Prospectus Department, 180 Varick Street, 2nd Floor, New York, NY 10014, or by email at prospectus@morganstanley.com.Today’s announcement does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy these securities, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation, or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction.

comments.textRawHtml:
Remember the dotcom? Do you remember companies like AltaVista or maybe pets.com?

Anthropic and OpenAI are the AltaVista of the AI era. With first starter advantage but no real moat and very good at spending money.

I am still waiting for the Google of this era to show its face.

Edit: every time I question these crazy valuations I get down voted really quickly.

children.author: JumpCrisscross
children.textRawHtml:
> Do you remember companies like AltaVista or maybe pets.com?

Compaq sold "83% of its AltaVista Internet search engine to CMGI Inc" for $2.3bn [1]. Four months later, ahead of its planned IPO, it disclosed $54mm in revenues [2]. 43x.

Pets.com IPO'd with $5.2mm of sales [3] and a $290mm valuation [4]. 56x.

Anthropic is going public at 40x trailing revenue (AltaVista territory) and 22x Q3 annualized revenue (not comparable).

> every time I question these crazy valuations I get down voted really quickly

You're the top comment. And this is against the guidelines: "Please don't comment about the voting on comments. It never does any good, and it makes boring reading" [5].

Pets.com was 15 months old at IPO, shutdown 9 months later

AltaVista was around 4yrs old when aquired and then CMGI IPO delayed and canceled

Anthropic is about 6 years old

children.author: greycol
children.textRawHtml:
The 'AI company' Allbirds is 11 years old... Putting out ages of business as if it reflects the maturity of the market or business is a little silly. AI harnesses as a general term basically emerged this year (open claw was first published in nov 2025). ChatGPT only released nov 2022 claiming ages longer than that reflects any form of stability seems beyond generous.

The better point is those companies listed never had a positive revenue before (or after) their IPO while Anthropic has had at least a few profitable quarters (though you'd really like a fiscal year to rule out the more obvious shenanigans). Though the bigger questions remain around the broader market and what that means for income and depreciation (amusingly because of the supply crunch the 'wildly optimistic' deprecation assumptions around GPUs that AI companies have been making have held true (technically you could argue they're appreciating assets, though that won't be the case if data centers start getting liquidated).)

children.author: swiftcoder
children.textRawHtml:
> And you need to factor in Anthropic's growth.

The problem with growth as a metric is that you can more-or-less linearly trade cash for growth. This is the same game that Uber and WeWork played, giving away product below market for years, in a straight trade of investor cash for growth

children.author: angoragoats
children.textRawHtml: That’s true; public sentiment about AI is already trending downward, and I suspect we’ll reach a point where these companies start experiencing steady negative growth, once people realize the tech is only ever going to be great for certain specific use cases (e.g. coding). So Anthropic seems equal to or worse than AltaVista from that perspective.
